meta.title: Dino USB Player - USB video player for Roku TV
meta.description: Dino USB Player is a Roku app for browsing and playing videos from an attached USB drive, with recursive video discovery, full-screen playback, subtitles, resume support, simple remote controls, and subscription options.

features.title: Features Built for Big-Screen USB Video Playback

cards.title: Made for Roku TV
bullets: Designed for Roku TV and simple remote control navigation
Two-pane home screen with a persistent side menu and USB video browser
Move between Reload Files, Subscribe, Settings, Help, About, Support, Privacy, and Terms
Back at the top level shows an exit confirmation instead of closing immediately

cards.title: USB Drive Browsing
bullets: Detects connected Roku external storage roots when a USB drive is available
Scans folders and subfolders recursively for video files
Shows loading, no-USB, and no-video states so the app status is clear
Reload Files returns the browser to the USB root and refreshes the library

cards.title: Video File Discovery
bullets: Lists video files only, keeping folders, images, audio, subtitles, and unknown files out of the visible browser
Recognizes MP4, AVI, MKV, MOV, FLV, WMV, WebM, M4V, 3GP, TS, MTS, M2TS, MPG, MPEG, VOB, and OGV extensions
Filters common hidden and system entries such as dot-prefixed names, lost.dir, System Volume Information, and $RECYCLE.BIN
Sorts videos alphabetically by file name with path used as a tie-breaker

cards.title: Full-Screen Video Player
bullets: Opens selected USB videos in a full-screen Roku video player
Custom transport overlay shows title, elapsed time, total duration, and progress
Use rewind 5 seconds, play/pause/replay, forward 5 seconds, subtitles, and More controls
Overlay auto-hides while video is playing and can be shown again with OK

cards.title: Remote-Friendly Playback Controls
bullets: Play remote key toggles play and pause
Replay remote key restarts playback
Back hides the visible controls before closing the player
Seeking is clamped safely between the beginning and known video duration

cards.title: Resume Playback
bullets: Saves progress while playing, when paused, and when closing the player
Resumes supported videos from the last saved position
Clears saved progress when a video finishes or is restarted
Skips resume records for very short videos, very early playback, and near-end positions

cards.title: Subtitle Support
bullets: Detects same-folder SRT, VTT, ASS, SSA, TTML, DFXP, and XML subtitle files
Shows a CC indicator in the USB browser when subtitles are available
Prioritizes subtitle files whose base name matches the selected video
Use the subtitle button to toggle one subtitle file or choose from multiple subtitle tracks

cards.title: Subtitle Language Detection
bullets: Builds Roku subtitle tracks with language, description, and track name metadata
Infers language markers from subtitle filenames when available
Recognizes common markers for English, Spanish, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Hindi, Japanese, Korean, and Chinese
Includes a Turn Off Subtitles option in the subtitle picker

cards.title: Free and Premium Access
bullets: Free users can try the first filename-sorted video from the USB browser
Videos beyond the free item show a centered lock overlay and subscription prompt
Free users can use subtitles for the first 20 minutes of each video when subtitles are available
Subscribed users unlock the full USB video library and extended subtitle access

cards.title: Roku Subscription Flow
bullets: Uses Roku ChannelStore purchase, recovery, and catalog flows
Subscription plans can show title, billing period, price, and free-trial text when provided
Subscribe prompts are available from locked video and subtitle-limit messages
Manage Subscription shows Roku account and device-side management instructions

cards.title: Settings and Playback Data
bullets: View screen resolution and screen aspect ratio
See available and total local storage information
Show USB storage size when a likely external USB volume is detected
Clear stored playback and resume records from Settings

cards.title: Help, Legal, and Support
bullets: Built-in Help/FAQ page with expandable questions
Privacy Policy and Terms of Use pages loaded from the Dino USB Player site
About page with app, developer, and version details
Support and feedback page with QR codes for Facebook support and feedback form links

cards.title: Local USB Design
bullets: Videos are read from your attached USB drive
The app is not a cloud storage, backup, or media hosting service
Playback compatibility depends on the file encoding and Roku device capabilities
Internet may be needed for Roku subscription, legal, support, and help links

items.a: Dino USB Player is a Roku app for finding and playing video files from an attached USB drive.

items.q: How do I start watching USB videos?
items.a: Connect a USB drive to your Roku device, open Dino USB Player, let it scan your drive, then choose a video from the USB browser.

items.q: Which video formats does it recognize?
items.a: The app recognizes common video extensions including MP4, MKV, AVI, MOV, WMV, FLV, WebM, M4V, 3GP, TS, MTS, M2TS, MPG, MPEG, VOB, and OGV.

items.q: Does it scan folders and subfolders?
items.a: Yes. Dino USB Player recursively scans folders and subfolders for video files.
Yes. The app detects subtitle files stored alongside videos and lets you enable, disable, or choose available subtitle tracks.

items.q: Does it remember where I stopped watching?
items.a: Yes. Dino USB Player can save and resume playback position for supported videos.
Free users can try the first video in the sorted USB library, and subtitle use may be limited to the first 20 minutes of each video.
A subscription unlocks the full USB video library and extended subtitle access.

items.a: Dino USB Player is a Roku app for browsing and playing videos from an attached USB drive.

items.q: Do I need a USB drive?
items.a: Yes. Dino USB Player is built around videos stored on a USB storage device connected to your Roku.
The visible browser lists video files only. Folders are scanned in the background so videos inside subfolders can still appear.
Yes. Supported subtitle files in the same folder can be detected and offered in the video player.
Yes. Dino USB Player saves playback progress and can resume supported videos from where you left off.
Free users can open the first filename-sorted video. Videos after the free item require a subscription.

items.q: Where do I manage my subscription?
items.a: Subscribed users can use Manage Subscription in the app, visit https://my.roku.com/subscriptions, or manage the app subscription from the Roku Home screen.
